(There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

General.md
# General Review Lessons

- Make a guard's zero-match check count only the matches it is meant to protect. Matches that are always present, like the guard's own allowed cases, keep the check from ever firing.
- Test a guard by planting a violation and by breaking its detection, and see it fail both times. A guard that passes on clean code proves nothing.
- Before acting on a review finding, check whether existing tests or contracts explain the current shape. A structural test can be why the code looks the way it does.
- When code reads a user-owned config into a typed struct and writes it back, keep the fields it does not model. Any new reason to rewrite the file otherwise silently deletes user data.
- Make a new outer timeout longer than every internal budget on that path. Otherwise the kill fires before the code's own graceful fallback.
- Before setting an explicit timeout, look up the platform's current default for that exact event; an explicit value can shorten the budget rather than add one.
- When splitting known from unknown JSON keys to preserve them, decode only the exact known keys and keep every other key, case variants included, as unknown. `encoding/json` matches field names case-insensitively, so decoding the whole object lets a key like `"Command"` overwrite the real field.
- When a change makes a fix command riskier or changes which command to run, update every place that tells the user to run it (status, doctor, help text). Otherwise one screen sends people to the safe fix and the next to the destructive one.
- When a test plants a failure to cover an error branch, make sure an earlier step doesn't fail first; otherwise the assertion passes without ever running that branch.
- Select an agent's final report by a marker it carries (such as the contract line), not by its position in the event stream; a trailing tool call or an empty message ID moves a position-based boundary.
# cli Review Lessons

- When replacing a git subprocess with a filesystem parser, check that it still works in bare repos and still respects exported `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`; git handles cases a parser misses.

I've started the review of PR #2549 in the background, and I'm waiting for it to finish.

While it runs, I read your review lessons. I'll check the diff against each one in `General.md` and `cli.md`. Two are especially relevant to this branch:
- Pick an agent's final report by its contract-line marker, not by where it sits in the event stream. Your recent commits are meant to do exactly this, so I'll check that the change follows it everywhere.

content.text:
I checked the top findings against the code. The review on PR #2549 (at `c512ab12d`) found two real bugs, and I confirmed both. I haven't edited anything.

## Confirmed bugs

**1. A reply with only a malformed contract line fails the post with a confusing error** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/trail_report.go:70-78`)
- **Trigger:** a reviewer replies with only `{"comments":null}`, or `{"comments":"none"}` with no summary.
- **Cause:** `decodeTrailComments` rejects anything that isn't an array, so `splitTrailJSON` returns no prose and `ok=false`. The run is marked unstructured. `combinedReviewNarratives` then parses the same text, gets no prose, and skips the run, so `Prose` ends up empty while `post` is still true.
- **Result:** `postReviewToTrail` (`review_bridge.go:59`) prints "Could not post the review to the trail: no review output to post".
- **Same gap on the judge path:** line 61 returns empty prose when the fallback narratives are also JSON-only.
- **Better outcome:** "Nothing to report", or a clear message that the output was malformed.

**2. The fallback posts the reviewer's whole output, not just its final report** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/cmd.go:1637-1641`)
- **Cause:** `trailReportFor` finds the report with `reportText(run.Buffer)`. When it marks a run unstructured, `combinedReviewNarratives` instead re-splits `joinAssistantText(run.Buffer)`, which is everything the reviewer wrote.
- **Trigger:** a reviewer explores ("I'll check:\n- retry.go"), writes `- [high] …` plus `{"comments":[]}`, then makes one more tool call and adds a closing line.
- **Result:** the contract line is no longer last, so it stays in the prose. The trail gets the exploration bullets as findings and the raw JSON in the body.
- **Lesson:** this is the same mistake as your General.md lesson about picking the report by its marker, not its position. The fix landed in one path but not the fallback.

## Plausible, but they're design calls

3. **Prose findings can be dropped** (`trail_report.go:65`, `:75`). When the contract line has comments, only those are posted, even if the prose lists more `[high]` bullets. Trusting the JSON may be on purpose, but the doc comment says a misbehaving model should cost an extra finding rather than a lost one.
4. **The "is this clean?" check misses some wordings** (`trail_report.go:191`). "Verdict: needs changes", "Findings:", "Problems:", `•` bullets, and `**High** foo.go:3` all count as clean when paired with `comments:[]`. The review's root-cause idea is an explicit `verdict` field in the contract line. That would replace the keyword list, but it's a larger change.

## Low priority
- **Duplicated detection:** severity and bullet detection in `startsWithSeverityMarker`/`isListItem` duplicates the helpers in `review_bridge.go` (`inferReviewTrailSeverity`, `splitReviewVerdictFindings`), and the lists already differ.
- **Contract line stripped outside trail mode:** `stripTrailJSON` also runs in local display and in the judge prompt. Real damage needs a reviewer to end on quoted JSON with a `summary` or `comments` key, which is unlikely.
- **Wasted tokens:** worker reviewers are asked for the contract line even when a judge will run. It's only used if the judge fails.
- **Slow TUI on long runs:** the detail view re-runs `stripTrailJSON` over every text block on each Pi delta, so the work grows quadratically.

I suggest fixing 1 and 2 on this branch. For 1, report nothing-to-post when there's no prose; for 2, use `reportText` in the fallback, falling back to the full buffer only when it returns "". If you agree, I'll write a detailed plan before changing anything. I'd also like your call on 3: should prose bullets be posted alongside the JSON comments?

No new review lessons: bug 2 is already covered by your existing lesson about picking the report by its marker.

content.text:
I tested each finding with throwaway tests against PR #2549 at `c512ab12d`. Three are real bugs, five reproduce but are either design calls or minor, and one is not a regression from this PR. The tests were added through `go test -overlay` and then deleted, and the working tree is clean.

## Real bugs

**1. A reply with only a malformed contract line fails the post with a confusing error.**
- **Inputs:** `{"comments":null}` and `{"summary":"","comments":"none"}`.
- **Result:** both the worker path and the judge path return `post=true` with 0 comments and empty prose.
- **Effect:** `postReviewToTrail` (`review_bridge.go:59`) rejects that report with "no review output to post", so the user sees "Could not post the review to the trail…".

**3. The fallback posts the reviewer's whole output, not just its report.** I ran the scenario all the way through `reviewTrailFindingInputs`. It posts three trail findings:
```
finding 0: "retry.go"
finding 1: "auth.go"
finding 2: "[high] foo.go:3 bug\n{\"summary\":\"none\",\"comments\":[]}\nDone."
```
The first two are exploration notes, not findings. The third carries the raw JSON and the closing text. The cause is that `combinedReviewNarratives` (`cmd.go:1640`) uses `joinAssistantText(run.Buffer)` instead of `reportText`.

**4. The clean check misses common ways of reporting findings.** `proseReportsFindings` returns false for all seven shapes tested:
- "Verdict: needs changes"
- "Blocking: …"
- "Findings:" followed by a paragraph
- "Problems:" followed by a paragraph
- `• foo.go:3`
- `### High` on its own line
- `**High** foo.go:3`

Any of these, paired with `"comments":[]`, posts nothing and prints "Nothing to report".

## Reproduces, but a design call or minor

- **2. Extra prose findings are dropped.** Three `[high]` bullets in the prose plus one JSON comment posts only that one comment, with empty prose. That holds for both the worker and judge paths. It contradicts the doc comment's promise that a misbehaving model costs an extra finding rather than a lost one, so it's your call whether that's intended.
- **5. Quoted JSON is stripped from display.** "The new endpoint returns:" followed by `{"summary":…,"comments":[…]}` loses the JSON in every display and in the judge prompt, including local mode. It needs a reviewer to end on JSON shaped exactly like the contract, which is unlikely.
- **7. Duplicated severity detection, more exact than the review said.** `startsWithSeverityMarker` (`trail_report.go:219`) is an almost line-for-line copy of `startsWithReviewSeverityMarker` (`review_bridge.go:302`). Sharing one copy means exporting it across the `review` and `cli` packages.
- **8. Workers get the JSON instruction even when a judge runs** (`cmd.go:1349`). This is true, but `trailReportFor` falls back to the worker output when the judge output is empty, so it acts as a working fallback. Only the token cost is real.
- **6. A `verdict` field in the contract line.** This is a design suggestion, so there was nothing to reproduce. It does address finding 4 at the root.

## Not a regression

- **9. Quadratic TUI work.** `refreshDetailContent` already rebuilt the whole buffer on every event before this PR. The PR adds a constant per-block cost for `stripTrailJSON`, which only unmarshals lines that start with `{`. The complexity doesn't change, so I'd drop this one.

My recommendation stands: fix 1 and 3 on this branch. For 4, either add the missed shapes or take the `verdict` field from finding 6, which is a bigger change but removes the keyword list. Which do you want, and should prose bullets be posted alongside the JSON comments (finding 2)?

There's also one possible review lesson: when a fix changes how one code path selects data, check every fallback path that re-derives the same data. Finding 3 is that miss. It may be close enough to your existing lesson about picking the report by its marker that you'd rather sharpen that one than add a new one.

content.content:
fix(review): don't post clean verdicts as Trail findings
fix-claude-review-stream-parser
Trail: https://entire.io/gh/MuskanPaliwal/cli/trails/12

When a reviewer approves a change with nothing to report, `entire review` posts that approval to the Trail as a finding. The Trail then shows an "Unspecified finding" for a review that found nothing.

`reviewTrailFindingInputs` looked for a runner-style JSON last line or Markdown finding bullets in the reviewer output. A clean approval such as

```text
approve - no actionable findings
```

has neither, so the fallback posted the whole output as one severity-less, whole-change comment.

This originally surfaced alongside a Claude stream parsing bug that made Codex the only successful reviewer. #2699 has since fixed the parser. The clean-verdict behavior is independent of it and still reproduces with any reviewer that returns a plain approval.

## What changed

Trail mode now asks for findings in a machine-readable form instead of interpreting verdict prose.

When `output` is `trail`, the reviewer and judge prompts end with a required JSON line:

```json
{"summary":"one-sentence verdict","comments":[{"severity":"high","body":"bug; impact; fix","location":{"granularity":"line","file_path":"path/to/file.go","start_line":42}}]}
```

The instruction is appended after profile and per-run text so neither can displace it, and it is skipped for a verbatim `prompt` override. The Markdown report stays as it was; the line is extra. Local runs do not ask for it.

Posting reads that line (`trail_report.go`):

- `"comments":[]` posts nothing and prints the existing "Nothing to report" notice, unless the prose contradicts it: a list item, severity marker, or feedback label such as `Nits:` at any indentation, or a `request changes` or `approve with nits` verdict, with or without a `Verdict:` label. Then the prose is posted as before.
- Comments post as native findings with their severity and location (line, range, file, or whole change). Entries without a body are dropped.
- When a judge runs, its line alone decides what is posted. The judge is asked to drop unsupported claims, so a reviewer's comment does not bypass it.
- Without a judge, each reviewer's final message is read separately and the comments are merged. The final message is the text after the reviewer's last tool call, which is the report the output format governs. Earlier narration such as "I'll check the changed files:" followed by a bulleted file list cannot contradict a clean final message. When the final message does contradict, the full narrative is posted as before.
- A missing or malformed line (no `comments` array) posts the prose with any trailing JSON removed, split into findings by top-level bullet. This is the previous behavior, so custom judge prompts that ignore the contract keep working. A JSON-only reply posts its `summary` rather than raw JSON.

When unsure, it posts. A false "clean" would hide a real finding, while a false "not clean" only restores the previous behavior.

The JSON line is kept in the saved manifest and hidden from reviewer dumps, the rendered judge verdict, and the `entire review --findings` list and detail views. The TUI event log still shows raw events, including the line.

`Deps.PostReviewToTrail` now takes a `TrailReport` (structured comments or prose, never both). The bridge maps comments straight to Trail finding inputs and drops its own last-line JSON parsing.

Streamed reviewer output needed one supporting change. `AssistantText` gains a `Delta` flag that marks a fragment continuing the previous text of the same message. Pi sets it for `message_update` fragments and resets at `message_end`, and `joinAssistantText` joins such fragments without a separator, so a JSON line split across fragments is still one line.

Earlier commits on this branch classified verdict prose with heuristics. The contract replaces that, so the branch's net diff has no prose classifier.

## Tests

- `review/trail_report_test.go`: judge JSON with empty, structured, fenced, pretty-printed, `null`, missing, and bodiless comments; a JSON-only reply with `null` comments posting its summary; empty JSON contradicted by a bullet, an indented bullet, a feedback label, or a non-clean verdict, and not contradicted by a labeled approve or a word that merely starts with a marker; the judge deciding over a reviewer's high-severity comment; single and multiple reviewers without a judge, including one reviewer without JSON; narration bullets before a tool call not contradicting a clean final message while a finding bullet after it still posts the whole narrative; streamed deltas joining into one parsable line and a new message starting a new line after a tool call; the instruction's own example line parsing; JSON stripped for display and from the `--findings` preview.
- `review/prompt_test.go` and `review/synthesis_prompt_test.go`: the contract is appended last in trail mode and absent otherwise.
- `review/posttrail_test.go`: posting, skipping, and error paths through `maybePostReviewToTrail` with the new report type.
- `review_bridge_test.go`: structured comments map to finding inputs; a whole-change prose verdict still posts as one `verdict`-kind finding.
- `agent/pi/reviewer_test.go`: text deltas carry the `Delta` flag only when continuing a message.

## Scope

This does not change reviewer failure policy, Trail API types, or server rendering. Prompts change only in trail mode.

fix(review): don't post clean verdicts as Trail findings
fix-claude-review-stream-parser
Trail: https://entire.io/gh/MuskanPaliwal/cli/trails/12

When a reviewer approves a change with nothing to report, `entire review` posts that approval to the Trail as a finding. The Trail then shows an "Unspecified finding" for a review that found nothing.

`reviewTrailFindingInputs` looked for a runner-style JSON last line or Markdown finding bullets in the reviewer output. A clean approval such as

```text
approve - no actionable findings
```

has neither, so the fallback posted the whole output as one severity-less, whole-change comment.

This originally surfaced alongside a Claude stream parsing bug that made Codex the only successful reviewer. #2699 has since fixed the parser. The clean-verdict behavior is independent of it and still reproduces with any reviewer that returns a plain approval.

## What changed

Trail mode now asks for findings in a machine-readable form instead of interpreting verdict prose.

When `output` is `trail`, the reviewer and judge prompts end with a required JSON line:

```json
{"summary":"one-sentence verdict","comments":[{"severity":"high","body":"bug; impact; fix","location":{"granularity":"line","file_path":"path/to/file.go","start_line":42}}]}
```

The instruction is appended after profile and per-run text so neither can displace it, and it is skipped for a verbatim `prompt` override. The Markdown report stays as it was; the line is extra. Local runs do not ask for it.

Posting reads that line (`trail_report.go`):

- `"comments":[]` posts nothing and prints the existing "Nothing to report" notice, unless the prose contradicts it: a list item, severity marker, or feedback label such as `Nits:` at any indentation, or a `request changes` or `approve with nits` verdict, with or without a `Verdict:` label. Then the prose is posted as before.
- Comments post as native findings with their severity and location (line, range, file, or whole change). Entries without a body are dropped.
- When a judge runs, its line alone decides what is posted. The judge is asked to drop unsupported claims, so a reviewer's comment does not bypass it.
- Without a judge, each reviewer's final message is read separately and the comments are merged. The final message is the text after the reviewer's last tool call, which is the report the output format governs. Earlier narration such as "I'll check the changed files:" followed by a bulleted file list cannot contradict a clean final message. When the final message does contradict, the full narrative is posted as before.
- A missing or malformed line (no `comments` array) posts the prose with any trailing JSON removed, split into findings by top-level bullet. This is the previous behavior, so custom judge prompts that ignore the contract keep working. A JSON-only reply posts its `summary` rather than raw JSON.

When unsure, it posts. A false "clean" would hide a real finding, while a false "not clean" only restores the previous behavior.

The JSON line is kept in the saved manifest and hidden from reviewer dumps, the rendered judge verdict, and the `entire review --findings` list and detail views. The TUI event log still shows raw events, including the line.

`Deps.PostReviewToTrail` now takes a `TrailReport` (structured comments or prose, never both). The bridge maps comments straight to Trail finding inputs and drops its own last-line JSON parsing.

Streamed reviewer output needed one supporting change. `AssistantText` gains a `Delta` flag that marks a fragment continuing the previous text of the same message. Pi sets it for `message_update` fragments and resets at `message_end`, and `joinAssistantText` joins such fragments without a separator, so a JSON line split across fragments is still one line.

Earlier commits on this branch classified verdict prose with heuristics. The contract replaces that, so the branch's net diff has no prose classifier.

## Tests

- `review/trail_report_test.go`: judge JSON with empty, structured, fenced, pretty-printed, `null`, missing, and bodiless comments; a JSON-only reply with `null` comments posting its summary; empty JSON contradicted by a bullet, an indented bullet, a feedback label, or a non-clean verdict, and not contradicted by a labeled approve or a word that merely starts with a marker; the judge deciding over a reviewer's high-severity comment; single and multiple reviewers without a judge, including one reviewer without JSON; narration bullets before a tool call not contradicting a clean final message while a finding bullet after it still posts the whole narrative; streamed deltas joining into one parsable line and a new message starting a new line after a tool call; the instruction's own example line parsing; JSON stripped for display and from the `--findings` preview.
- `review/prompt_test.go` and `review/synthesis_prompt_test.go`: the contract is appended last in trail mode and absent otherwise.
- `review/posttrail_test.go`: posting, skipping, and error paths through `maybePostReviewToTrail` with the new report type.
- `review_bridge_test.go`: structured comments map to finding inputs; a whole-change prose verdict still posts as one `verdict`-kind finding.
- `agent/pi/reviewer_test.go`: text deltas carry the `Delta` flag only when continuing a message.

## Scope

This does not change reviewer failure policy, Trail API types, or server rendering. Prompts change only in trail mode.

content.text:
Nothing in the diff is out of scope; every file supports the PR's goal of not posting clean verdicts as Trail findings. The findings divide into ones to fix here and ones to defer.

## The diff itself
Each change exists to keep clean approvals off the Trail:
- the JSON contract and the prompts that ask for it;
- `trailReportFor`, which decides what gets posted;
- the bridge's new `TrailReport` type;
- the Pi `Delta` flag, so a contract line split across stream fragments still parses;
- the code that hides the contract line from display.

The `synthesisPromptOptions` struct is a small refactor, but only because the judge prompt needed a fourth parameter. I found no unrelated cleanups.

The PR description is out of date in three places:
- It says a reviewer's report is "the text after the reviewer's last tool call". Since `99a7c1ffb` and `c512ab12d`, the report is found by its contract line instead.
- It says the TUI event log still shows the contract line. `tui_detail.go:70` now hides it in the detail view.
- It says the net diff "has no prose classifier", but `proseReportsFindings` is one. It only decides whether the prose contradicts an empty comments array, but reviewers will see it as a classifier.

## Findings to fix in this PR
This PR introduced each of these:
- **1. A reply with only a malformed contract line fails the post with an error.** This is new behavior from `trailReportFor`.
- **3. The fallback posts the whole buffer.** The PR changed how the report is selected but not the fallback path.
- **4. The clean check misses ways of reporting findings.** It's the PR's own check, and a miss loses findings, which the PR promises won't happen.
- **2. Prose findings are dropped when JSON comments exist.** This is the PR's own policy, and it contradicts the PR's "when unsure, it posts" promise. You'll need to decide whether that's intended.
- **7. Duplicated severity detection.** The PR added the copy of `startsWithReviewSeverityMarker`.

## Out of scope
- **6. A `verdict` field in the contract.** This is a contract redesign. It's worth a follow-up issue unless you'd rather solve finding 4 with it.
- **8. Token cost of the worker JSON instruction.** It works as a fallback by design, so this is only a cost tradeoff.
- **9. TUI rebuild cost.** The full rebuild on every event predates this PR.
- **5. Hiding quoted JSON outside trail mode.** This is technically in scope, but it's unlikely enough to leave as a note.

For this PR I'd fix 1, 3, 4 (by adding the missed shapes), and 7, decide on 2, and refresh the description. Findings 6, 8, and 9 can go in a follow-up issue if you want them tracked.

content.text:
The out-of-scope items are saved in `.bare/worktrees/fix-claude-review-stream-parser/OUT_OF_SCOPE.md`. It's local to this worktree and not in the repo. I can turn it into a GitHub issue later if you want.

Here's the plan for 1, 3, 4, 2 and 7. I've reproduced each finding (see above) and haven't edited anything yet.

## 1. A reply with only a malformed contract line fails the post
- **Cause:** for a JSON-only reply like `{"comments":null}`, `trailReportFor` returns `post=true` with no comments and no prose. `postReviewToTrail` then rejects it with "no review output to post".
- **Change:** in `maybePostReviewToTrail` (`cmd.go:1608`), when the report is empty, print *"The review produced no readable report, so nothing was posted to the trail."* and return. "Nothing to report" would be wrong here, since the model didn't actually say the change is clean.

## 3. The fallback posts the whole buffer instead of the report
- **Cause:** `combinedReviewNarratives` uses `joinAssistantText(run.Buffer)`.
- **Change:** use `reportText(run.Buffer)` first, and fall back to the full buffer only when it returns "" (no valid contract line). That keeps the old behavior for reviewers that ignore the contract.
- **Tests that change:** two existing tests assert the current shape.
  - "a finding bullet in the final message posts the whole narrative" will instead assert that only the report is posted, with no exploration bullets.
  - "a new message starts a new line after a tool call" exists to check line joining. I'll drop the JSON from its final message so it takes the full-buffer path and still tests that.

## 4. The clean check misses ways of reporting findings
- **Cause:** fixed prefix lists in `proseReportsFindings`.
- **Change:** add every shape that reproduced:
  - `• ` bullets;
  - a severity marker alone on a line, or followed by closing emphasis, which covers `### High` and `**High** foo.go:3`;
  - verdict wording "needs changes", "needs work", "changes needed" and "blocking";
  - labels `findings:` and `problems:`.
- **Tradeoff:** "Findings: none" will count as not clean and post its prose. `Issues:` already behaves that way, and it's the safe direction: an extra finding, not a lost one.
- **Not doing here:** the bigger fix, a `verdict` field in the contract, stays in the out-of-scope note.

## 2. Prose findings are dropped when JSON comments exist
- **Cause:** any non-empty comments array wins over the prose.
- **Why not post both:** the prompt asks for the Markdown report *and* the JSON line, so the prose normally repeats every comment. Posting both would duplicate each finding.
- **Change:** count the severity-marked finding lines in the prose, meaning bullets or lines starting with `[high]`, `[medium]`, `[low]` and so on. If there are more of them than JSON comments, treat the JSON as incomplete and post the prose instead. That's the existing prose path, which the bridge splits into findings and fills in severity and location where it can.
- **Tradeoff:** in that case the findings lose the exact locations the JSON carried. Exploration bullets with no severity marker aren't counted.

## 7. Duplicated severity detection
- **Change:** keep one copy of severity-marker and list-item detection in the `review` package, exported, and have the bridge's `topLevelMarkedFindingText`/`topLevelBulletText` call it. The bridge keeps its own top-level-only rule.
- **Effect:** the posting check and the prose splitter now agree. That includes the new shapes from fix 4, so `• ` bullets and `**High**` lines will also split into separate findings.
- **Not touched:** `inferReviewTrailSeverity` and `normalizeReviewTrailSeverity` map text to a severity value. They do a different job, so they stay as they are.

## Order and verification
1. Write the failing tests first: subtests in `trail_report_test.go`, plus a bridge test for the shared splitting. Run them to confirm each one fails for the expected reason.
2. Fix the code.
3. Run `mise run check`.

After that I'll show you the commit message and an updated PR description, which also corrects the three stale claims, before anything is pushed.

Should I go ahead?

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

content.text:
All five fixes (1, 2, 3, 4 and 7) are in, and the tests that cover them pass. Nothing is committed or pushed yet.

**Verification**
- **New tests:** the 14 new or changed subtests all failed before the fix for the expected reasons, and all pass now. The `review` and `review/types` packages pass in full.
- **Lint and docs:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint` reports 0 issues, and `go test ./docs/development` passes.
- **Canary:** all 4 deterministic E2E tests pass.
- **Integration:** 53 tests pass. `TestExternalCommand_SigintReachesPlugin` failed once in the full integration run and passed when rerun alone, so it looks flaky. It doesn't touch the review code.
- **Unrelated failures:** `TestCheckpointListPending_Preview*` (3 tests) and `TestPreviewNextCheckpoint` also fail on an untouched copy of `HEAD`. Their fixtures hard-code a session started on 2026-10-07, which is now a week old. So `mise run check` will fail until someone fixes that on `main`. I've left it alone because it's outside this PR.
- **Not verified:** a real `entire review` run posting to a Trail, because that makes paid agent calls. The tests go through `maybePostReviewToTrail`, the actual posting decision, with the hook stubbed.

**What changed**
- **Finding 1:** an empty report now prints *"The review produced no readable report, so nothing was posted to the trail."* instead of failing the post.
- **Finding 3:** the fallback posts the reviewer's report, not its whole buffer. A reviewer with no valid contract line still posts its full narrative.
- **Finding 4:** the clean check now catches `•` bullets, `### High`, `**High** …`, "needs changes", "needs work", "changes needed", and the `Findings:`, `Problems:` and `Blocking:` labels.
- **Finding 2:** if the prose has more severity-marked findings than the JSON line has comments, the prose is posted instead.
- **Finding 7:** there's now one shared `StartsWithSeverityMarker`/`ListItemText` in the `review` package, used by both the posting check and the bridge's splitter. The bridge's copy is deleted.
- **Docs:** `docs/architecture/review-command.md` is updated to match.

**Proposed commit message**
```
fix(review): post findings an incomplete or unreadable trail contract would lose

A reviewer whose report contradicted its empty JSON line had its whole
event buffer posted, so exploration bullets became findings and the raw
JSON landed in the prose. Post only the report it ended with the contract
line; a reviewer without a valid line still posts its whole narrative.

A JSON line with fewer comments than the prose's severity-marked findings
dropped the rest. Post the prose instead, since it normally repeats every
comment.

A JSON-only reply with nothing readable reached the trail hook as an
empty report and failed with "no review output to post". Say that the
review produced no readable report instead.

The clean check missed "needs changes" verdicts, Findings:/Problems:/
Blocking: labels, unicode bullets, and heading or bold severity markers.
Severity and list-item detection now live in one place, shared by the
posting check and the bridge's prose splitter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**PR description:** the only changes are to the **What changed** bullets, the paragraph about where the line is hidden, the paragraph about earlier commits, and **Tests**. The full new text:

````markdown
Trail: https://entire.io/gh/MuskanPaliwal/cli/trails/12

When a reviewer approves a change with nothing to report, `entire review` posts that approval to the Trail as a finding. The Trail then shows an "Unspecified finding" for a review that found nothing.

`reviewTrailFindingInputs` looked for a runner-style JSON last line or Markdown finding bullets in the reviewer output. A clean approval such as

```text
approve - no actionable findings
```

has neither, so the fallback posted the whole output as one severity-less, whole-change comment.

This originally surfaced alongside a Claude stream parsing bug that made Codex the only successful reviewer. #2699 has since fixed the parser. The clean-verdict behavior is independent of it and still reproduces with any reviewer that returns a plain approval.

## What changed

Trail mode now asks for findings in a machine-readable form instead of interpreting verdict prose.

When `output` is `trail`, the reviewer and judge prompts end with a required JSON line:

```json
{"summary":"one-sentence verdict","comments":[{"severity":"high","body":"bug; impact; fix","location":{"granularity":"line","file_path":"path/to/file.go","start_line":42}}]}
```

The instruction is appended after profile and per-run text so neither can displace it, and it is skipped for a verbatim `prompt` override. The Markdown report stays as it was; the line is extra. Local runs do not ask for it.

Posting reads that line (`trail_report.go`):

- `"comments":[]` posts nothing and prints the existing "Nothing to report" notice, unless the prose contradicts it: a list item (including `•`), a severity marker (including a `### High` heading or `**High**`), a feedback label such as `Nits:` or `Findings:` at any indentation, or a non-approving verdict such as `request changes`, `approve with nits`, or `needs changes`, with or without a `Verdict:` label. Then the prose is posted as before.
- Comments post as native findings with their severity and location (line, range, file, or whole change). Entries without a body are dropped. If the prose has more severity-marked findings than the line has comments, the line is incomplete and the prose is posted instead. The prose normally repeats every comment, so posting both would duplicate them.
- When a judge runs, its line alone decides what is posted. The judge is asked to drop unsupported claims, so a reviewer's comment does not bypass it.
- Without a judge, each reviewer's report is read separately and the comments are merged. The report is the last stretch of text between tool calls that ends with a valid line, found by that line rather than by position, so a trailing tool call does not hide it. Earlier narration such as "I'll check the changed files:" followed by a bulleted file list cannot contradict a clean report. When the report does contradict its line, that report is posted; a reviewer with no valid line posts its whole narrative, as before.
- A missing or malformed line (no `comments` array) posts the prose with any trailing JSON removed, split into findings by top-level bullet. This is the previous behavior, so custom judge prompts that ignore the contract keep working. A JSON-only reply posts its `summary` rather than raw JSON. When nothing readable is left, nothing is posted and the run says the review produced no readable report.

When unsure, it posts. A false "clean" would hide a real finding, while a false "not clean" only restores the previous behavior.

The posting check and the bridge's prose splitter share one severity-marker and list-item detector, so prose judged to have findings also splits into them.

The JSON line is kept in the saved manifest and hidden from reviewer dumps, the rendered judge verdict, the live TUI detail view, and the `entire review --findings` list and detail views.

`Deps.PostReviewToTrail` now takes a `TrailReport` (structured comments or prose, never both). The bridge maps comments straight to Trail finding inputs and drops its own last-line JSON parsing.

Streamed reviewer output needed one supporting change. `AssistantText` gains a `Delta` flag that marks a fragment continuing the previous text of the same message. Pi sets it for `message_update` fragments and resets at `message_end`, and `joinAssistantText` joins such fragments without a separator, so a JSON line split across fragments is still one line.

Earlier commits on this branch classified verdict prose with heuristics. The contract replaces that. What remains is a fail-open check that only decides whether the prose contradicts an empty or incomplete comments array.

## Tests

- `review/trail_report_test.go`: judge JSON with empty, structured, fenced, pretty-printed, `null`, missing, and bodiless comments; a JSON-only reply with `null` comments posting its summary, and one with nothing readable not reaching the hook; empty JSON contradicted by a bullet, an indented or unicode bullet, a feedback label, a severity heading or bold marker, or a non-clean verdict, and not contradicted by a labeled approve, a word that merely starts with a marker, or a bold word after one; comments missing a severity-marked prose finding posting the prose; the judge deciding over a reviewer's high-severity comment; single and multiple reviewers without a judge, including one reviewer without JSON; narration bullets before a tool call not contradicting a clean report, while a finding bullet in the report posts only that report, not the narration or text after a trailing tool call; streamed deltas joining into one parsable line and a new message starting a new line after a tool call; the instruction's own example line parsing; JSON stripped for display and from the `--findings` preview.
- `review/prompt_test.go` and `review/synthesis_prompt_test.go`: the contract is appended last in trail mode and absent otherwise.
- `review/posttrail_test.go`: posting, skipping, and error paths through `maybePostReviewToTrail` with the new report type.
- `review_bridge_test.go`: structured comments map to finding inputs; unicode bullets and bold severity lines split into separate findings; a whole-change prose verdict still posts as one `verdict`-kind finding.
- `agent/pi/reviewer_test.go`: text deltas carry the `Delta` flag only when continuing a message.

## Scope

This does not change reviewer failure policy, Trail API types, or server rendering. Prompts change only in trail mode.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
````

I checked the diff against your review lessons in `General.md` and `cli.md` and found no violations. One possible new lesson for `General.md`: *"When a fix changes how one path selects data, update every fallback that selects the same data; otherwise the fallback keeps the old bug."* Since it's close to your existing lesson about picking the report by its marker, it might work better as a sharper version of that one.

Can I commit with this message, push, and update the PR description to this text? After the push I'll check the Trail findings as the repo requires.
